paragraph: No stage is set. [In September 2017 Banco Nacional de Angola's Aviso 7/17 set transparency, information and contract rules for payment service users](<https://lex.ao/docs/banco-nacional-de-angola/2017/aviso-n-o-7-17-de-12-de-setembro/>). [In September 2016 Aviso 12/2016 set rules for marketing financial products and services, payment-service providers' included](<https://angop.ao/noticias/economia/bna-reforca-supervisao-das-instituicoes-financeiras/>). [The bank's ranking put Afrimoney, a mobile money platform, at 1,138 complaints in the second quarter of 2025, up 180% on the first quarter](<https://pti.ao/afrimoney-lidera-queixas-de-clientes-das-instituicoes-financeiras-nao-bancarias/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says consumer-protection rules for digital financial services are drafted or in force. Establishing would need such rules in force.

No stage is set. Nothing has been found since October 2023 that says whether consumer-protection rules apply to digital financial services in Burundi. No rule, draft or complaints body for digital finance has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying that no consumer-protection rules apply to digital financial services.

No stage is set. [A 2020 decree created the OQSF, an observatory that mediates for financial-sector clients](<https://fraternite.bj/guichets-automatiques-bancaires-et-mobile-money-enquete-sur-le-calvaire-des-usagers-face-aux-transactions-echouees/>). [The client may obtain mediation through the OQSF, operational since October 2024](<https://fraternite.bj/guichets-automatiques-bancaires-et-mobile-money-enquete-sur-le-calvaire-des-usagers-face-aux-transactions-echouees/>). [On 29 July 2025 the OQSF presented an online portal for complaints from financial-sector clients](<https://leconomistebenin.bj/benin-un-nouveau-portail-en-ligne-pour-les-plaintes-financieres/>), and [it covers e-money issuers' customers](<https://leconomistebenin.bj/benin-un-nouveau-portail-en-ligne-pour-les-plaintes-financieres/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says consumer-protection rules for digital finance are drafted or in force. Establishing would need such rules in force.

[The OQSF-BF, created by decree in December 2022, offers financial mediation in disputes between users and providers](<https://www.finances.gov.bf/fileadmin/user_upload/storage/Etude_diagnostique_mecanismes_de_recours_interne_des_PSF_Rapport_Final.pdf>). E-money issuers are among the providers. [BCEAO Instruction n°001-01-2024 requires e-money issuers to run complaint-handling systems for clients and merchants](<https://www.finances.gov.bf/fileadmin/user_upload/storage/Etude_diagnostique_mecanismes_de_recours_interne_des_PSF_Rapport_Final.pdf>). [In 2025 the observatory was merged into the national financial-inclusion agency, ANPFI](<https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article148215>). In the last twelve months, [in October 2026 the OQSF-BF, housed in ANPFI, said it mediates free of charge in disputes with e-money issuers and other providers](<https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article149951=>). No source found reports a fine, a sanction or complaint figures after 2022. Mature would need such figures or a sanction under these rules.

[The Bank of Botswana says the Electronic Payment Services (Amendment) Regulations, 2026, took effect on 2 April 2026](<https://www.bankofbotswana.bw/sites/default/files/press-release-files/Implementation%20of%20the%20Electronic%20Payment%20Services%20%28Amendment%29%20Regulations%2C%202026.pdf>). [They include market conduct obligations to enhance consumer protection](<https://www.bankofbotswana.bw/sites/default/files/press-release-files/Implementation%20of%20the%20Electronic%20Payment%20Services%20%28Amendment%29%20Regulations%2C%202026.pdf>). The regulations took effect in the last twelve months, and no earlier consumer rule for digital finance has been found. No source found since October 2023 says a financial ombudsman or complaints unit takes complaints. Operating would need a financial ombudsman or a regulator's complaints unit that takes complaints about digital financial services.

[In June 2025 the OQSF-CI's secretary said the observatory handles complaints about e-money issuers among others](<https://www.lemeridien.ci/amelioration-de-la-gouvernance-economique-lobservatoire-de-la-qualite-des-services-financiers-presente-aux-populations-dagboville/>). [Consumers can complain to the OQSF-CI by green line, email or website](<https://infocentrale.net/2025/07/05/entretien-zoom-sur-les-plateformes-digitales-pour-saisir-loqsf-en-cote-divoire/>). In the last twelve months, [from 2 November 2026 the regional central bank capped fees on PI-SPI instant transfers](<https://launchbaseafrica.com/2026/11/03/failed-transfers-hidden-fees-and-phantom-aliases-inside-the-messy-birth-of-west-africas-unified-payments-network/>). Transfers are free up to 8,000 CFA francs a day, and the fee is 0.8 per cent above that. [On 4 November 2026 a National Assembly committee adopted a banking bill covering fintech and e-money institutions](<https://www.linfodrome.com/economie/127262-banques-fintech-monnaie-electronique-la-cote-d-ivoire-prepare-une-nouvelle-reglementation>). It provides for complaints handling, mediation and a deposit guarantee. No fine or sanction under these rules has been found. Mature would need a fine, sanction, licence withdrawal or complaint figures for digital financial services.

[CEMAC Regulation 01-20 of 3 July 2020 protects consumers of banking services](<https://obs-cc.org/fraude-mobile-money-cameroun-sensibilisation-ne-suffit-pas/>). It provides for complaint services and mediation. In the last twelve months, [in October 2026 the consumer observatory OBS-CC said the regulation also applies to payment institutions](<https://obs-cc.org/fraude-mobile-money-cameroun-sensibilisation-ne-suffit-pas/>). [OBS-CC added that Regulation 04/18 requires a permanent complaints mechanism for payment services](<https://obs-cc.org/fraude-mobile-money-cameroun-sensibilisation-ne-suffit-pas/>). No source found since October 2023 says a financial ombudsman or regulator's complaints unit in Cameroon takes digital finance complaints. Operating would need such a body to take them.

No stage is set. The nearest instruments found are [Décret n° 2024-86 du 28 février 2024 portant institution de la médiation financière](<https://kalieu-elongo.com/un-pas-de-plus-vers-leffectivite-de-la-mediation-financiere-au-congo/>) and [Règlement N° 01/20/CEMAC/UMAC/COBAC du 3 juillet 2020 (protection des consommateurs de produits et services bancaires)](<https://www.artf.cg/storage/download/publications/BItvf6e7Xn80iUaSDhSpbs0O7rXv7M7JzxxC4fqc.pdf>). Nothing found since October 2023 says whether consumer-protection rules apply to digital finance in Congo. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need consumer-protection or conduct rules covering digital financial services in force.

[The central bank's 2024 conduct report applies Decree-Law 8/2018](<https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2025/RSC%202024.pdf>), the legal regime for payment services and electronic money. Under it banks refunded clients for unauthorised card and internet-banking transactions. [A Banco de Cabo Verde official said in March 2025 that the central bank handles complaints about digital payment systems](<https://www.asemana.cv/index.php/atualidade/14109-maior-parte-das-fraudes-acontece-por-uso-indevido-dos-sistemas-de-pagamentos-digitais-bcv>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. [In 2024 the central bank recorded 10 internet-banking complaints among 169 against banks](<https://www.bcv.cv/SiteCollectionDocuments/2025/RSC%202024.pdf>), and banks refunded complainants 3.25 million escudos.

[Bank of Algeria Instruction 06-2025 of 17 August 2025 requires payment service providers to keep customer funds in segregated escrow accounts](<https://launchbaseafrica.com/2025/08/19/algeria-opens-for-fintech-new-psp-rules-create-a-playbook-for-payments-startups/>). It also requires a bank guarantee or liability insurance, and that users accept a contract setting out fees and dispute procedures before an account opens. [In October 2024 the Bank of Algeria said it was drafting a regulation to protect consumers of financial services, notably digital ones](<https://algerie-eco.com/2024/10/09/protection-des-consommateurs-des-services-financiers-un-reglement-sera-promulgue-avant-fin-2024/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No financial ombudsman or central bank complaints unit for digital financial services has been found. Operating would need one that takes complaints about digital financial services.

[The Central Bank of Egypt's instructions of 7 May 2024 set minimum requirements for complaint handling by banks, covering complaints about banks, outsourcing providers, payment service providers and agents contracted by the bank](<https://www.cbe.org.eg/ar/laws-regulations/regulations/regulations-book/book-14/chapter-2>). [On 19 February 2019 the CBE issued customer-rights instructions for banks and providers such as mobile payment companies, Shalakany says](<https://shalakany.com/new-regulations-on-the-protection-of-bank-customers/>). [Compliance was due by February 2020](<https://shalakany.com/new-regulations-on-the-protection-of-bank-customers/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a financial ombudsman or a regulator's complaints unit takes complaints about digital financial services. Operating would need such a body.

[In March 2026 the National Bank of Ethiopia said its Financial Consumer Protection Directive No. FCP/01/2020 requires financial institutions to tell customers about fraud risks](<https://nbe.gov.et/announcements/>). In the last twelve months, [an assessment of the second National Financial Inclusion Strategy was reported by The Reporter in October 2026](<https://www.thereporterethiopia.com/53174/>). It says the strategy set up a dedicated financial consumer protection directorate that handles complaints. [The same auditors cautioned that consumer safety mechanisms remain ill-equipped for digital fraud, scams and social-engineering risks](<https://www.thereporterethiopia.com/53174/>). No source found reports a fine, sanction, licence withdrawal or complaint figures for digital financial services. Mature would need such a report.

[CEMAC Regulation 01/20 of 3 July 2020, a decree of 21 March 2024 and two ministerial orders of 7 January 2025 set Gabon's financial mediation framework](<https://www.echosdeleco.com/articles/mediation-financiere-le-gabon-lance-officiellement-son-dispositif-le-26-octobre>). [It covers payment institutions and mobile money disputes](<https://www.echosdeleco.com/articles/mediation-financiere-le-gabon-lance-officiellement-son-dispositif-le-26-octobre>). [UNCDF's November 2023 diagnostic said a new regulation on digital financial consumer protection was expected](<https://www.uncdf.org/Download/AdminFileWithFilename?cultureId=127&filename=2023-diagnostic-gabon-finalpdf&id=20054>). In the last twelve months, the mediation scheme was due to launch on 26 October 2026. No source found says it has begun taking complaints. Operating would need a financial ombudsman or a regulator's complaints unit that takes complaints about digital financial services.

[The Bank of Ghana says the Directive for Digital Credit Service Providers (September 2025) is in force](<https://www.bog.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Notice-No.25-BOG-SEC-GOV-2026-Notice-PUBLICATION-OF-UNLICENSED-DIGITAL-CREDIT-SERVICE-PROVIDERS-ON-THE-BANKS-WEBSITE-SOCIAL-MEDIA-PLATFORMS-AND-OTHER-COMM-CHANNELS-1.pdf>). [Its Second Deputy Governor said it requires digital credit providers to be licensed, disclose loan terms and follow consumer protection rules](<https://www.graphic.com.gh/business/business-news/ghana-news-bog-eoco-crack-down-on-400-illegal-online-lenders.html>). [In October 2025 the Bank said it had shut down more than 400 illegal online lending operators](<https://www.graphic.com.gh/business/business-news/ghana-news-bog-eoco-crack-down-on-400-illegal-online-lenders.html>). [Its 2023 complaints report counts 23 complaints against payment systems and service providers](<https://www.bog.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/2023-COMPLAINTS-MANAGEMENT-REPORT_Publication.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [on 17 November 2026 the Bank of Ghana named 19 loan apps operating in breach of the directive](<https://www.bog.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Notice-No.45-BOG-SEC-GOV-2026-Notice-PUBLICATION-OF-UNLICENSED-DIGITAL-CREDIT-SERVICE-PROVIDERS-ON-THE-BANKS-WEBSITE-SOCIAL-MEDIA-PLATFORMS-AND-OTHER-COMM-CHANNELS-1.pdf>).

[The central bank's instruction I/DGSIF/DSIMF/006/2018 sets consumer-protection standards for inclusive financial institutions, e-money institutions among them](<https://actuguinee.net/institutiins-financieres-inclusives-microfiances-et-autres-les-clients-sont-ils-vraiment-proteges-me-fode-mourana-soumah/>). Fees must be displayed, contracts written and language plain. Clients have access to their own data. In the last twelve months the instruction was cited and not changed. [In August 2026 the lawyer Fodé Mourana Soumah described what the standards give clients of e-money services and other institutions](<https://actuguinee.net/institutiins-financieres-inclusives-microfiances-et-autres-les-clients-sont-ils-vraiment-proteges-me-fode-mourana-soumah/>). No source found since October 2023 names a financial ombudsman or a regulator's complaints unit. Operating would need such a body to take complaints about digital financial services.

[In April 2025 the Ministry of Trade was revising the Competition and Consumer Protection Acts](<https://alkambatimes.com/stakeholders-endorse-gccpc-study-on-digital-market-competition-and-consumer-welfare/>), [working with a consultant, the GCCPC and Commonwealth support](<https://alkambatimes.com/stakeholders-endorse-gccpc-study-on-digital-market-competition-and-consumer-welfare/>). [The revision addresses digital markets, including e-commerce and digital financial platforms](<https://alkambatimes.com/stakeholders-endorse-gccpc-study-on-digital-market-competition-and-consumer-welfare/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says consumer-protection rules for digital financial services are in force. Establishing would need consumer-protection or conduct rules covering digital financial services or digital lending in force.

[The Competition Authority of Kenya received 355 complaints from borrowers about digital lenders in the year to June 2025](<https://www.businessdailyafrica.com/bd/economy/complaints-about-digital-lenders-jump-five-times--5528224>). The year before there were 67. [Amendments to the CBK Act brought non-deposit-taking digital lenders under Central Bank of Kenya supervision](<https://www.itweb.africa/article/kenya-licenses-29-new-digital-lenders/KzQenqjyjp2MZd2r>). By September 2026, 281 digital credit providers were licensed. In the last twelve months, [seven Kenyan regulators issued a draft Financial Consumer Protection Framework, with comments due 28 April 2026](<https://www.ca.go.ke/sites/default/files/CA/Public%20Consultation/Consumer%20Protection%20Framework%20March%202026.pdf>). [The Central Bank of Kenya says its draft National Payment System Bill, 2026 aims to secure consumer and data protection](<https://www.centralbank.go.ke/2026/09/21/draft-national-payment-system-policy-and-national-payment-system-bill-2026/>).

No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether consumer-protection rules apply to digital finance in Liberia. The nearest items found are [Liberia Telecommunications Authority consumer protection services](<https://newspublictrust.com/lta-begins-decentralizing-its-regulatory-and-consumer-protection-services>) and [MTN Mobile Money](<https://www.micat.gov.lr/media/lina-daily-news-bulletin/monrovia-june-15-lina-lonestar-cell-mtn-mobile-money-inc-prominent>). No rule, complaints unit or complaint figure for digital financial services has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says no consumer-protection rules apply to digital financial services.

No stage is set. [In March 2020 the National Payments Council issued an e-payment services regulation under the Central Bank of Libya](<https://cbl.gov.ly/en/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%8A%D9%94%D8%AD%D8%A9-%D8%AE%D8%AF%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AF%D9%81%D8%B9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%95%D9%84%D9%83%D8%AA%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86%D9%8A.pdf>). [Its consumer protection chapter requires e-payment and mobile-wallet providers to give clear written service information, honest advertising and call-centre support](<https://cbl.gov.ly/en/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%8A%D9%94%D8%AD%D8%A9-%D8%AE%D8%AF%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AF%D9%81%D8%B9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%95%D9%84%D9%83%D8%AA%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86%D9%8A.pdf>). [In June 2025 the Central Bank of Libya launched the website of its instant payment service, LYPay, with a platform for submitting complaints and inquiries](<https://cbl.gov.ly/en/the-central-bank-of-libya-officially-launches-the-website-for-the-instant-payment-service-lypay/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says consumer-protection rules for digital finance are drafted or in force. Establishing would need such rules in force.

[In February 2026 a Central Bank of Lesotho official said the Financial Consumer Protection Act of 2022 requires providers to lend responsibly and safeguard customer information](<https://newsdayonline.co.ls/cbl-tightens-financial-customer-protection-efforts/>). [The Central Bank of Lesotho's Financial Consumer Protection Division handles and resolves financial complaints](<https://newsdayonline.co.ls/cbl-tightens-financial-customer-protection-efforts/>). In May 2025 the government told a parliamentary committee that the [Payment Systems Bill, 2025 enforces consumer protection measures for payments](<https://nationalassembly.parliament.ls/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Report-Payment-Systems-Bill-2025.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [in February 2026 the market conduct framework was still being finalised](<https://newsdayonline.co.ls/cbl-tightens-financial-customer-protection-efforts/>). No source found since October 2023 reports a fine, a sanction or complaint figures for digital financial services. Mature would need such a report.

No stage is set. [In 2024 Al Wassit Albanki, the banking mediation centre set up under Bank Al-Maghrib, received 5,536 complaint files](<https://cmmb.ma/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Rapport-dactivite-2024.pdf>). [Payment institutions and money transfer companies were among the institutions concerned](<https://cmmb.ma/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Rapport-dactivite-2024.pdf>). [The mediation rules of the Centre Marocain de Médiation Bancaire, of 23 March 2023](<https://cmmb.ma/la-mediation-2/reglement-de-mediation-al-wassit-al-banki/>), bind its members, payment institutions among them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says consumer-protection rules for digital finance are drafted or in force. Establishing would need such rules in force.

[Under the 2020 banking law the CSBF regulates e-money institutions, ensures user protection and can sanction breaches up to withdrawal of licence](<https://newsmada.com/2026/08/28/telecommunications-et-monnaie-electronique-le-csbf-joue-aussi-le-role-de-lautorite-de-controle/>). [E-money institutions are legally required to run a 24/7 customer service handling complaints on loss, theft, fraud and unauthorised transactions, per 2424.mg](<https://2424.mg/mobile-money-les-autorites-annoncent-des-audits-du-systeme-des-etablissements-de-monnaie-electronique/>). Oral complaints must be confirmed in writing within five working days. In the last twelve months the law was cited and not changed: [in August 2026 Newsmada reported the CSBF's role over e-money institutions](<https://newsmada.com/2026/08/28/telecommunications-et-monnaie-electronique-le-csbf-joue-aussi-le-role-de-lautorite-de-controle/>). No source found since October 2023 says a financial ombudsman or a regulator's complaints unit takes complaints about digital financial services. Operating would need such a body.

[Since 2 November 2026 new tariff rules of the regional central bank cap the fees on some electronic payment operations](<https://fr.apanews.net/technologies/mali-sama-money-ouvre-la-reception-des-paiements-instantanes-de-luemoa/>), APA reports. In the last twelve months, [the Malian e-money issuer SAMA Money made receiving instant transfers free](<https://fr.apanews.net/technologies/mali-sama-money-ouvre-la-reception-des-paiements-instantanes-de-luemoa/>) in November 2026. The fee rules come from the regional central bank, and no earlier consumer rule for digital finance in Mali has been found. No source found says an ombudsman or a regulator's unit takes complaints about digital financial services in Mali. Operating would need such a body.

[The instant payment system (SPIM) regulation took effect on 2 March 2026](<https://www.bancomoc.mz/media/1bwihts1/aviso-1-gbm-2026.pdf>). It [sets a complaints procedure with an electronic portal](<https://www.bancomoc.mz/media/1bwihts1/aviso-1-gbm-2026.pdf>). [In April 2025 Banco de Moçambique put out for consultation a revision of its notice protecting mobile money customer funds](<https://www.bancomoc.mz/en/media/highlights/public-consultation-on-the-proposed-revision-of-the-notice-that-establishes-measures-for-protecting-customer-funds-received-in-exchange-for-mobile-money/>). In the last twelve months, [in the first half of 2026 the bank received 44 complaints about mobile money](<https://bancomoc.mz/media/ofiltvbv/dsc_comunicado_estati-sticas-das-reclamac-o-es-recebidas-no-banco-de-moc-ambique-contra-instituic-o-es-financeiras-no-i-semestre-de-2026_v01_en.pdf>). Of these, [26 were against Vodafone M-Pesa and 18 against M-Mola](<https://bancomoc.mz/media/ofiltvbv/dsc_comunicado_estati-sticas-das-reclamac-o-es-recebidas-no-banco-de-moc-ambique-contra-instituic-o-es-financeiras-no-i-semestre-de-2026_v01_en.pdf>). [Across all complaints in that half-year the bank issued directives for correction](<https://bancomoc.mz/media/ofiltvbv/dsc_comunicado_estati-sticas-das-reclamac-o-es-recebidas-no-banco-de-moc-ambique-contra-instituic-o-es-financeiras-no-i-semestre-de-2026_v01_en.pdf>). They included [the refund of MZN 73,243,072 in improperly charged fees](<https://bancomoc.mz/media/ofiltvbv/dsc_comunicado_estati-sticas-das-reclamac-o-es-recebidas-no-banco-de-moc-ambique-contra-instituic-o-es-financeiras-no-i-semestre-de-2026_v01_en.pdf>).

No stage is set. In the last twelve months, the central bank announced a pilot week of its complaints call centre for April 2026. Nothing found shows it taking complaints. Nothing found names rules for digital finance, a regulator's complaints unit for digital financial services, or complaint figures. Absent would need a source from the past three years that says no consumer-protection rules apply to digital financial services.

[The Reserve Bank of Malawi issued a directive setting complaint-handling procedures for banks and other providers](<https://times.mw/reserve-bank-of-malawi-tightens-grip-on-financial-sector/>). It sets resolution within 2 to 30 days and penalties up to K50 million per institution. [The Reserve Bank says its fintech regulatory framework is meant to ensure consumer protection](<https://mwnation.com/fintech-push-spurs-rbm-to-rethink-monetary-tools/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. [The Deputy Governor said 36,481 complaints about digital payments were recorded from April 2023 to March 2024](<https://times.mw/reserve-bank-of-malawi-demands-seamless-digital-payment-systems/>). [The 2024 annual report counts 46,969 banking-sector complaints linked to failed digital financial services](<https://times.mw/financial-consumer-complaints-increase/>).

[The Bank of Namibia's determination PSD-1 took effect on 6 January 2026](<https://www.bon.com.na/CMSTemplates/Bon/Files/bon.com.na/31/313b4ab5-b138-45d3-b526-28959686db96.pdf>). [It carries user protection requirements for payment service providers](<https://www.bon.com.na/CMSTemplates/Bon/Files/bon.com.na/31/313b4ab5-b138-45d3-b526-28959686db96.pdf>), [at paragraphs 10.4 and 16 of its arrangement of paragraphs](<https://www.bon.com.na/CMSTemplates/Bon/Files/bon.com.na/31/313b4ab5-b138-45d3-b526-28959686db96.pdf>). The determination took effect in the last twelve months, and no earlier consumer rule for digital finance has been found. No source found since October 2023 says a financial ombudsman or complaints unit takes complaints. Operating would need a financial ombudsman or a regulator's complaints unit that takes complaints about digital financial services.

[In January 2024 UNCDF said Niger's consumer protection texts do not cover digital finance](<https://www.uncdf.org/fr/article/8603/vers-une-meilleure-protection-des-consommateurs-au-niger>). [It said they need updating](<https://www.uncdf.org/fr/article/8603/vers-une-meilleure-protection-des-consommateurs-au-niger>). It also said practically no legal recourse exists for consumers of digital financial services. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says consumer rules for digital finance are being drafted. Preparing would need consumer-protection rules for digital financial services to be drafted.

[The FCCPC's Digital, Electronic, Online or Non-Traditional Consumer Lending Regulations 2025 have been in force since 21 July 2025](<https://fccpc.gov.ng/fccpc-resumes-digital-lending-regulation/>). They set consumer-protection rules for all digital lenders. [The FCCPC invites consumers to report unlawful or unregistered digital lenders to its complaint portal](<https://fccpc.gov.ng/digital-lending-fccpc-tackles-abuses-issues-landmark-regulations/>). In the last twelve months, [on 21 January 2026 the FCCPC began enforcement, withdrawing conditional approval from digital lenders that missed the compliance deadline](<https://fccpc.gov.ng/digital-lending-rule-fccpc-goes-after-violators/>). [TechCabal reports MTN suspended its airtime lending in April 2026 under a regulatory suspension linked to the FCCPC's new requirements](<https://techcabal.com/2026/08/24/mtn-sees-nigeria-rebound-as-airtime-lending-returns/>). The Federal High Court upheld the regulations on 20 July 2026.

[NBR says customers with unresolved eKash problems may complain to the National Bank of Rwanda through the Intumwa chatbot](<https://www.bnr.rw/documents/Press_Release-_Update_on_the_Performance_of_eKash_Aug_2026.pdf>). They can reach it by SMS, WhatsApp, website and social media. In the last twelve months, [in August 2026 NBR took eKash complaints through its Intumwa chatbot](<https://www.bnr.rw/documents/Press_Release-_Update_on_the_Performance_of_eKash_Aug_2026.pdf>). [Governor Hakuziyaremye says the consumer-protection framework requires failed transfers to be refunded in a timely manner](<https://www.ktpress.rw/2026/10/bnr-moves-to-tackle-delayed-ekash-transfers/>). No source found since October 2023 reports a fine, sanction or complaint figures. Mature would need a fine, sanction, licence withdrawal or complaint figures for digital financial services.

[Central Bank of Sudan Circular 7/2026 sets binding minimum rules for USSD financial services](<https://cbos.gov.sd/ar/node/24567/>). They cover fee disclosure, no debit on failed transactions, free SMS confirmations, 24-hour support and complaint resolution within 48 hours. In the last twelve months, [in July 2026 the central bank revoked the e-payment licence of Al-Asjad Digital and Smart Solutions](<https://sudanhorizon.com/cbos-officially-revokes-al-asjad-companys-license-following-review/>), acting under its licensing standards and not under the consumer rules. No source found since October 2023 names a financial ombudsman or a regulator's unit that takes complaints about digital financial services. Operating would need such a body.

[The Observatoire de la qualité des services financiers settles disputes between users and providers by mediation](<https://aps.sn/mediation-financiere-475-dossiers-traites-en-2025-contre-379-en-2024-oqsf/>). It has been under the Ministry of Finance since 2009. [It handled 475 new disputed files in 2025, against 379 in 2024](<https://aps.sn/mediation-financiere-475-dossiers-traites-en-2025-contre-379-en-2024-oqsf/>). These figures cover all financial services. In the last twelve months, [from 2 November 2026 the regional central bank capped fees on PI-SPI instant transfers](<https://launchbaseafrica.com/2026/11/03/failed-transfers-hidden-fees-and-phantom-aliases-inside-the-messy-birth-of-west-africas-unified-payments-network/>). Transfers are free up to 8,000 CFA francs a day, and the fee is 0.8 per cent above that. No source found reports a fine, sanction, licence withdrawal or complaint figures for digital financial services. Mature would need such a report.

[In July 2025 the National Communications Authority presented a proposed quality-of-service framework for digital financial services, to be applied jointly with the Bank of Sierra Leone](<https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-T/Workshops-and-Seminars/qos/20250701/Documents/2-Melvin%20King.pdf>). Its consumer provisions set timeframes for resolving complaints and require disclosure of service terms. [The Bank of Sierra Leone's 2022–2026 financial inclusion strategy says its Consumer Protection Section tracks complaints, and that mobile money providers report complaints to the bank](<https://afi-global.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Sierra-Leone-NSFI-2022-2026_FINAL_Final.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says consumer-protection rules for digital financial services are in force. Establishing would need such rules in force.

[In November 2025 the House of the People passed the National Payment System Bill](<https://golekaab.so/en/bill/15>). [The bill is stated to ensure consumer protection](<https://golekaab.so/en/bill/15>). [It awaits the Senate](<https://golekaab.so/en/bill/15>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says consumer-protection rules for digital financial services are in force. Establishing would need consumer-protection or conduct rules covering digital financial services or digital lending in force.

[In September 2025 the Bank of South Sudan issued a consumer protection notice](<https://jakony.com/digital-money-operators-face-new-security-and-reporting-rules/>) that [covers banks, microfinance institutions and digital financial service providers](<https://jakony.com/digital-money-operators-face-new-security-and-reporting-rules/>). [It requires clear fee and loan disclosure and complaint contacts, and bars harassment and fraudulent deductions](<https://jakony.com/digital-money-operators-face-new-security-and-reporting-rules/>). In the last twelve months, [in September 2026 consumer protection rules took effect under the amended Electronic Money Regulation](<https://radioyei.org/news/technology/boss-sets-strict-usd-caps-on-mobile-money/>), and [they cover banks and non-bank e-money issuers](<https://radioyei.org/news/technology/boss-sets-strict-usd-caps-on-mobile-money/>). No source found since October 2023 says a financial ombudsman or complaints unit takes complaints. Operating would need a financial ombudsman or a regulator's complaints unit that takes complaints about digital financial services.

No stage is set. Nothing has been found since October 2023 that says whether consumer-protection rules apply to digital financial services in Sao Tome and Principe. No rule, draft or complaints body for digital finance has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying that no consumer-protection rules apply to digital financial services.

[Since 5 March 2019 a Central Bank of Eswatini practice note has set rules for mobile money providers](<https://www.centralbank.org.sz/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/PracticeNoteforMMSP-FinalMarch2019.pdf>), [covering fee disclosure, written customer contracts and complaints handling](<https://www.centralbank.org.sz/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/PracticeNoteforMMSP-FinalMarch2019.pdf>). [In October 2024 the World Bank called these consumer-protection requirements limited](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099082525170036534/pdf/P505756-da939ce0-36a3-4072-9fbb-8f90280267ab.pdf>) and said banks and mobile money providers generally comply with them. [The Central Bank of Eswatini says consumers can escalate complaints to the CBE's Ombudsman](<https://www.centralbank.org.sz/market-conduct-consumer-protection-unit/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports a fine, sanction, licence withdrawal or complaint figures for digital financial services. Mature would need such a report.

[From 1 January 2025 the Financial Consumer Protection (Complaint Handling) Regulations 2024 apply to all financial services providers in the Act's Schedule](<https://www.gazette.sc/sites/default/files/2025-01/SI%20110%202024%20-%20Financial%20Consumer%20Protection%20%28Complaint%20Handling%29%20Regulations%202024.pdf>). [Digital finance is not named](<https://www.gazette.sc/sites/default/files/2025-01/SI%20110%202024%20-%20Financial%20Consumer%20Protection%20%28Complaint%20Handling%29%20Regulations%202024.pdf>). [The Financial Consumer Protection Act came into force on 1 May 2022, with a six-month transition](<https://www.cbs.sc/Consumer/ConsumerLaws.html>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. [In 2025 the Central Bank received 50 complaints directly from customers of banks and payment service providers](<https://www.cbs.sc/Downloads/ConsumerProtection/ComplaintsData/Consumer%20Complaints%20Data%20-H1%20and%20H2%202025.pdf>). [The Central Bank of Seychelles reports that payment service providers received 25 complaints in 2025](<https://www.cbs.sc/Downloads/ConsumerProtection/ComplaintsData/Consumer%20Complaints%20Data%20-H1%20and%20H2%202025.pdf>), 14 in the first half and 11 in the second.

[In July 2026 leconomie.info set out the CEMAC payment-institution rules Moov Money Tchad must meet to keep its licence](<https://leconomie.info/tchad-moov-money-rejoint-le-club-restreint-des-etablissements-de-paiement-agrees/>). [It must ring-fence client funds and meet solvency norms](<https://leconomie.info/tchad-moov-money-rejoint-le-club-restreint-des-etablissements-de-paiement-agrees/>), and [it must also run regular cybersecurity audits](<https://leconomie.info/tchad-moov-money-rejoint-le-club-restreint-des-etablissements-de-paiement-agrees/>). The report dates from the last twelve months, and no earlier position has been found. No source found since October 2023 says a financial ombudsman or complaints unit takes complaints. Operating would need a financial ombudsman or a regulator's complaints unit that takes complaints about digital financial services.

[Central Bank of Tunisia Circular No. 2024-2 is dated 29 January 2024](<https://www.tunisiaonlinenews.com/tunisia-cyber-risk-who-pays-when-electronic-payments-fail/>). [It governs the information given to clients on the marketing and pricing of financial products and services](<https://www.tunisiaonlinenews.com/tunisia-cyber-risk-who-pays-when-electronic-payments-fail/>), and [it covers remote operations](<https://www.tunisiaonlinenews.com/tunisia-cyber-risk-who-pays-when-electronic-payments-fail/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says a financial ombudsman or complaints unit takes complaints, or reports a fine, sanction or complaint figures. Operating would need a financial ombudsman or a regulator's complaints unit that takes complaints about digital financial services.

[The Bank of Tanzania Financial Consumer Protection (Amendment) Regulations, GN No. 298 of 2025, are dated 23 May 2025](<https://kemiadvocates.co.tz/2025/06/27/legal-update-key-highlights-of-the-bank-of-tanzania-financial-consumer-protection-amendment-regulations-gn-no-298-of-2025-date-23-may-2025>). Kemi Advocates reports they set fee disclosure, fraud-loss refund and complaint-handling rules for all providers the bank supervises, mobile money included. [The bank's financial consumer protection department takes unresolved complaints about banks, microfinance institutions and mobile money providers](<https://dailynews.co.tz/bot-complaint-system-cuts-financial-disputes/>). It received over 1,500 complaints in 2024. [On 21 November 2024 the Bank of Tanzania named 69 digital lending apps as unlicensed and in breach of its guidance note](<https://www.bot.go.tz/Adverts/PressRelease/en/2024112512091545.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [in April 2026 the finance minister said fees on interoperability transfers between wallets and bank accounts are capped at 5,000/- for amounts above 500,000/-](<https://www.ippmedia.co.tz/the-guardian/news/local-news/read/interoperability-costs-cut-while-113-agencies-operate-payments-systems-2026-04-28-111407>).

[In March 2024 the Uganda Microfinance Regulatory Authority launched its Digital Lending Guidelines](<https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/online-lenders-harassing-borrowers-risk-closure-4645060>), which set conduct rules for online lenders on confidentiality, interest limits, harassment and complaints redress. [Since September 2022 payment licensees have followed conduct, disclosure and complaint rules under the National Payment Systems (Consumer Protection) Regulations](<https://media.ulii.org/media/legislation/74619/source_file/4ebccd52d76b1b54/ug-act-si-2022-103-publication-document.pdf>). [The Bank of Uganda's Financial Consumer Empowerment Mechanism takes complaints about supervised financial institutions left unresolved for 21 days](<https://govinfohub.go.ug/index.php/2024/04/29/bou-details-redress-procedure-for-aggrieved-bank-customers/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Mature would need a fine, sanction, licence withdrawal or complaint figures for digital financial services under these rules.

[The National Credit Act's affordability assessment applies to credit providers, digital lenders among them](<https://financialregulationjournal.co.za/2026/02/18/credit-risk-and-affordability-in-south-african-credit-regulation-distinguishing-two-assessments-in-a-digital-credit-environment/>), a Financial Regulation Journal article said in February 2026. Debt review and findings of reckless lending are the remedies. [The National Financial Ombud's banking division reports that mobile banking and internet banking fraud generated the most complaints in 2025, 39% of all cases received](<https://nfosa.co.za/nfo-banking-division-returns-r60-million-to-consumers-in-2025/>). [The ombud closed 3,651 fraud cases in 2025, most of them in mobile and digital banking](<https://www.citizen.co.za/business/fraud-complaints-at-the-banking-ombud-nearly-double-in-a-year-as-digital-scams-surge/>). In the last twelve months the credit rules were cited and not changed. No fine, sanction or licence withdrawal for digital financial services has been found. Mature would need one under these rules.

[Directives in force since 2 August 2024 ban listed e-money wallet fees and cap others](<https://regalert.today/document/directives-on-unwarranted-charges-and-fees-on-electronic-money-services-bca3f339-2d82-4256-967c-905e4917c5f1>). [On 14 September 2024 the Bank of Zambia issued directives against unwarranted e-money charges](<https://www.zambiamonitor.com/bank-of-zambia-cracks-down-on-unwarranted-charges-for-electronic-money-services/>), and [an e-money institution in breach faces a fine of up to K200,000 or up to two years' imprisonment](<https://www.zambiamonitor.com/bank-of-zambia-cracks-down-on-unwarranted-charges-for-electronic-money-services/>). [The Competition and Consumer Protection Commission resolved 1,477 complaints in 2024](<https://www.zambiamonitor.com/consumer-protection-commission-claims-1477-complaints-resolved-in-2024/>), and [the main ICT complaint was delayed or unreversed mobile money transactions](<https://www.zambiamonitor.com/consumer-protection-commission-claims-1477-complaints-resolved-in-2024/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 reports a fine or sanction under the e-money directives. Mature would need a fine, sanction, licence withdrawal or complaint figures for digital financial services under these rules.

[In February 2026 the governor said the bank continued to receive complaints from the public about the cost of banking](<https://www.newsday.co.zw/local-news/article/200052094/rbz-cuts-limits-bank-charges-expands-mobile-and-zipit-limits>).
